timeline_reviews.summary: Transport-only serial Claude CLI stream; no semantic events projected, accounted as transport evidence only.
Serial parent trajectory: single actor explored docs, generated ELF fixtures, probed HTML/CLI/ELF edge cases extensively, but never wrote a replacement workspace implementation before timeout.

parallel.requirements: Recognized the task as a behavioral clean-room reimplementation of elfcat 0.1.10, including CLI flags, ELF parsing, HTML report generation, and prohibitions on source lookup, wrapping, and disassembly.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership but launched a single workflow containing 12 exhaustive probe children for p_type, sh_type, flags, number formatting, notes, string tables, byte order, ascii/dump rules, bitness, JS, errors, and sections.
parallel.implementation: The parent extracted static report assets and wrote a Rust Cargo project with main.rs, elf defs/parser, and report text/dump modules, while consuming some child reports from /tmp/findings.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The submitted artifact included the partial Rust source tree and assets plus original workspace files, but no completed buildable replacement executable; artifact validation and evaluation both failed.
parallel.verification: The parent ran many behavioral probes and read findings, but there is no final cargo build/test or evaluator-aligned acceptance pass before timeout; official evaluation reported compile_failed with all tests not run.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with ptype, numfmt, strtab, and sections still in progress and errors failed; the parent source tree remained incomplete and uncompiled at closure.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same behavioral reverse-engineering task and stayed within local observation of the executable and bundled documentation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor performed all exploration, fixture generation, probing, and intended implementation work without workflow, task, or agent delegation.
serial.implementation: The serial run built extensive temporary Python ELF generators and probes under /tmp, but did not create replacement source files in the submitted workspace before timeout.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The artifact contained only the original repository files, license, readme, git metadata, and executable, so there was no integrated reimplementation to compile.
serial.verification: The serial run produced extensive observed behavior evidence and final stdout/stderr checks, but no replacement implementation or integrated build verification.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: It timed out during probing, produced an empty final response, and official evaluation reported compile_failed with all tests not run.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified the clean-room behavioral reimplementation requirement and probed CLI, ELF, and HTML behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same requirement and performed behavioral probing without disallowed external source or binary analysis evidence.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the outcome; both failed despite understanding the task constraints.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed discovery into 12 child probe tasks while the parent retained implementation ownership and wrote source files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used no delegation and kept all probing and potential implementation in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent budget across many research children; serial had no coordination overhead but also never reached implementation delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs were detailed and asked for exhaustive Markdown findings in /tmp/findings, with a common toolkit and known facts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated findings inline through its own shell probes and did not have handoff or child interface boundaries.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a large findings handoff surface and several unavailable reports, while serial had no cross-agent context boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel wrote a Rust project and partial modules for parsing and report rendering after extracting template assets.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial created probing helpers and temporary fixtures but did not write submitted workspace source files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel got farther toward a reimplementation but left it incomplete; serial remained a probe-only attempt by closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received several child reports and read many of them, but the workflow ended killed with multiple progress children and one error.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle; all observations stayed in the parent trajectory until timeout.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure included unfinished child lifecycle state; serial closure had no join or child-result failure mode.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used shared /tmp/findings outputs and parent-owned workspace source writes; no concrete write collision is shown, but integration stayed partial.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used /tmp scratch fixtures and submitted no new implementation files, leaving the artifact as the original workspace contents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had partial final-tree integration work; serial had no implementation tree to integrate.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed many behavioral probes but no final build or integrated acceptance evidence; official evaluation completed with compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed many behavioral probes and final stream checks, but no buildable replacement; official evaluation also completed with compile_failed.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both lacked evaluator-aligned acceptance of a replacement executable; parallel had a partial source tree, serial had none.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel used 13 subagents, 448 tool calls, 1.1M workflow-child tokens, and timed out after the workflow remained killed/incomplete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used 100 tool calls, no workflow child tokens, and timed out after a long sequential probing run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a distinct child fan-out budget burden; serial exhausted its budget sequentially without coordination overhead.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both official evaluations completed and both failed with compile_failed, so there is no discordant official outcome to explain. The concrete task-solving difference is process and artifact shape: parallel created a partial Rust implementation while an expansive child-probe workflow remained killed/incomplete; serial did extensive single-agent probing but never wrote a replacement implementation. Neither delivered a buildable solution, and all 646 tests were not run in both evaluations.
parallel_contributors: Broad child probe fan-out consumed substantial budget and left several required findings unfinished or errored.
Parent implementation remained partial and was not build-verified before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial actor spent the run on probing and temporary fixtures without creating submitted source files.
No delegation overhead occurred, but the single-agent implementation stage still did not happen before timeout.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel artifact contained a partial Rust source tree; serial artifact contained no replacement source tree.
Both artifacts failed before any test execution, so behavioral correctness differences were not measured.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: Both fail; the retained pattern is a directly evidenced parallel adverse process, not an explanation for a pass/fail divergence.

Rejected: the observed allocation problem was not a narrow underallocation to one critical worker; it was the collective breadth of the 12-child fan-out.

The parent launched a 12-agent exhaustive probing workflow while it still had to finish implementation, build, and verify. The workflow state records one retry, one failed child, multiple children still in progress, killed status, and 1.1M child tokens; the parent left only a partial Rust tree and the official evaluator reported compile_failed. Serial had no delegation and no workflow child budget, so this is a parallel-side adverse process rather than the reason for a discordant outcome.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad child fan-out consumed the available parallel budget and closed with unfinished/error probes, leaving implementation and build verification incomplete; the submitted artifact failed compilation with all tests not run.
candidates.near_match_reason: Although several completed probe reports were long, the direct failure boundary was collective fan-out and unfinished children; the parent actually read several reports, and other required results were absent rather than merely too bulky to consume.
